subject: HyperPod Labs – deployment topology, SLA targets, and next steps (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hyperpod.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: HyperPod Labs – deployment topology, SLA targets, and next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap to make sure we captured the core constraints and to lay out next steps. If I misstate anything, flag it and we’ll update.

Pain points you mentioned:
- Model latency spikes during peak scraping windows (10–11am PT) causing end-user timeouts (~1–2% of requests).
- Monthly token costs are higher than expected because of long context windows (avg 1,400 tokens per request).
- Audit/retention requirement: 90 days of request/response metadata in a customer-managed S3.

Goals you want to achieve in the next 90 days:
1) Stable P95 latency <= 220ms for single-turn generation under expected peak throughput (120 qps).
2) Reduce token cost per request by at least 25% without degrading output quality.
3) Proof-of-concept on Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS integration for audit trail access.

Technical notes from our convo (high level):
- Target model: LLaMA-3-20B/quantized variant for generative recommendations.
- Typical sequence lengths: request 400 tokens, generation 600 tokens (scope for prefix caching).
- Current infra: 4x GPUs (mixed A100/RTX) behind a K8s-based inference cluster. You’re open to a hybrid approach (Dedicated for peak, Hosted for burst).

Attachments I’ll share: initial topology sketch, SLO matrix draft, and a Dedicated pricing summary (attached).

Immediate next steps (what I’ll do):
- Marcus to produce a preliminary deployment topology and kernel/quantization suggestion by EOW (he’ll call out required GPU types).
- I’ll share the SLO matrix and a short ROI calc for the 25% cost reduction plan.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week with your infra lead (Grace to coordinate times).

What we need from you:
- Confirmation of peak qps window(s) and a 7-day request histogram (timestamps + sequence lengths).
- Any regulatory constraints for logs beyond the 90-day S3 requirement.
- Preferred dates/times for tech deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: hyperpod-topology-v1.png; slo-matrix-hyperpod.xlsx; redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf

Cc: HyperPod Labs Procurement <procurement@hyperpod.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HyperPod Labs – deployment topology, SLA targets, and next steps (post-call recap)

Hannah —

Thanks for the clean summary. A few clarifications:
- Peak qps is closer to 140 in the 10–11am PT window on weekdays; nights drop to ~20 qps.
- Sequence lengths: request 350–450 tokens (mode ~380), generation trimmed to 500 on average currently.
- We do require access logs for 180 days for a subset of customers (enterprise tier), but metadata-only 90 days for others.

Procurement ping: procurement@hyperpod.io is evaluating the Dedicated pricing sheet — can you include any available short-term committed pricing for a 6-month pilot?

I’ll pull the 7-day histogram and upload to the shared Drive link once I have it (aiming to send by Mon 19 Apr).

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of ML Infrastructure
HyperPod Labs
daniel.park@hyperpod.io
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hyperpod.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HyperPod Labs – deployment topology, SLA targets, and next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Daniel —

Following up with a technical sketch and preliminary recommendations (see attached topology image and SLO matrix). Short summary here:

1) Deployment topology suggestion (pilot / Dedicated):
- Control plane: Redwood-managed in-hosted control plane with VPC peering to HyperPod (dedicated control channel).
- Serving plane: 2x Dedicated GPU pools for peak (each pool: 8x H100s or 16x A100-80GB alt), autoscaling disabled for pilot, manual burst policy enabled to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
- Fallback: Redwood Hosted smaller model pool (quantized LLaMA-3-7B) in us-west to handle overflow requests for soft degradation.

2) Latency and throughput SLOs (preliminary):
- P50 target: <= 80ms token production during steady state.
- P95 target: <= 220ms end-to-end for single-turn gen at 140 qps.
- P99 target: <= 600ms; overage triggers alert and automatic fallback to smaller model variant.

3) Cost / quality levers:
- Quantization path: recommend int8+KV cache preservation to keep quality while cutting per-token GPU time.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache 70–80% of repeat prefixes during the peak scraping window to reduce compute.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with a 15ms max latency gate to ensure latency SLOs.

4) Data retention / security:
- We can push request/response metadata to your S3 with server-side KMS; for enterprise 180-day subset, we provision a dedicated retention bucket and lifecycle policy.

Open items I’ll confirm after we see the 7-day histogram:
- Expected distribution of sequence lengths (so we can size KV cache and choose kernel paths).
- Request arrival pattern for the 10–11am peak (bursty vs sustained) to size Dedicated pool.
- Your preference on H100 vs A100 in pilot (cost vs latency).

Attachments: hyperpod-topology-v1.png (annotated), slo-matrix-hyperpod.xlsx (with P50/P95/P99 columns).

I’m available Tue/Thu next week for a 60-minute deep dive; Hannah — can you propose slots?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hyperpod.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, HyperPod Labs Procurement <procurement@hyperpod.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HyperPod Labs – deployment topology, SLA targets, and next steps (post-call recap)

Daniel — quick update and confirmations:

1) Marcus will lead the technical deep-dive on Tue 27 Apr at 10am PT — invite sent.
2) Action items for HyperPod: please upload the 7-day histogram and mark which customers require 180-day retention by Mon 26 Apr.
3) Procurement: attached is a short-term committed pricing addendum for a 6-month pilot (redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf). We included a pilot discount tier if you commit to reserved capacity for the peak window.

If that all looks good I’ll get the pilot order form drafted and loop legal for a quick review.

Best,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
